facts.raw_span: intermittent palpitations for 2 days
no history of chest pain, dyspnea, congestion, or fever
no past cardiac history or family history of similar complaints
Blood pressure was 110/72 mm Hg
respiratory rate was 14 bpm
Cardiovascular system examination results were unremarkable
Wide complex tachycardia at rate of 190 bpm
atypical left bundle branch morphology (QS in leads V1-V5 with transition in V6)
QRS duration of 146 ms with no evidence of AV dissociation
Global hypokinesia of right ventricle, dilated RV, ballooned out RVOT measuring 35 mm
RV ejection fraction of 19.3%
Postcontrast hyperenhancement along RV free wall, RVOT apical wall, RV aspect of septum, and in basal inferior, midcavity inferior, and inferoseptal myocardium of left ventricle

concepts.why: The patient's ECG and imaging studies show characteristic features of ARVC, including wide complex tachycardia, global hypokinesia of the right ventricle, and postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall.
The patient's ECG shows a wide complex tachycardia at a rate of 190 bpm, which is consistent with VT.
The patient's ECG and imaging studies show features consistent with RVOT tachycardia, including a wide complex tachycardia and a ballooned out RVOT.
The patient's imaging studies show a dilated right ventricle and a low RV ejection fraction, which are consistent with DCM.
The patient's imaging studies show postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall, which is consistent with CS.
The patient's imaging studies show a dilated right ventricle and a low RV ejection fraction, which are consistent with RVD.
It explains the atypical left bundle branch morphology found in the ECG studies.

rationales.F11: Reduced RV ejection fraction is a characteristic feature of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and right ventricular dysfunction.
rationales.F12: Postcontrast hyperenhancement along the RV free wall is a characteristic feature of arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy and cardiac sarcoidosis.
